text:
If you were hoping to salvage Sunday outdoors, the rain has made the decision for you so far, with fog, mist, and a chilly 54 degrees at midday. Keep the wet-weather gear handy this afternoon, as rain should linger with temperatures barely reaching the upper 50s. The breeze may gust near 25 mph, and the lake is running rough enough that I’d stay off the broad water.

Rain should taper by early evening, with only a slight leftover chance before 7, then a mostly cloudy, cool night dropping toward 47. The lake settles tonight, but it builds again Monday as north winds strengthen, with waves back to 1 to 3 feet. Burlington gets a mostly cloudy, seasonably cool Monday near 61, and the bigger story is the start of a dry stretch. Keep today’s plans close to home, then look for a better outdoor window Monday, especially away from the water.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): High pressure will bring a reinforcing shot of cool air on Monday. It will be partly sunny but unseasonably cool with highs only in the 50s. A few lucky ones may break into the low 60s. Monday night will have good radiational cooling with lows ranging from the 20s to low 40s. Frost and even a freeze are possible in parts of the region, especially the Adirondacks and Northeast Kingdom, so you’ll want to prepare to protect any crops you want to save. Stay tuned for updates. Fall officially arrives on Tuesday, and it will feel like it with slightly warmer but still-cool highs in the upper 50s to low 60s. At least we’ll get to enjoy mostly sunny skies.
